context.identity_boundary: Reusable encrypted storage business meaning: immutable objects, storage bindings, retrieval and failures; provider and runtime selection remain separate.
context.owner_ref: CyberAlchemy v2 Knowledge Exchange Protocol product owner
context.purpose: For one exact encrypted Knowledge Artifact Version or recipient-specific key envelope, persist immutable bytes under an exact durable-storage policy, verify retrieval against their qualified content identity before dependent use, and emit environment-bounded evidence without exposing plaintext, keys, credentials, or provider identity as object identity.

limitations: Source construction and evidence postures remain preserved; not promoted to Lab admission.
Source declares no relation role signatures; validation covers explicit meanings and endpoint closure only.
Source proof requirements remain evidence requirements, not newly executed tests.
Context profile_ref points to source ontology metadata; not an admitted execution profile.

boundaries: Source Product meaning only; Lab admission and operational authority remain separate.
All relationship endpoints resolve within this source graph; no external concepts merged.
ontology.name: Durable encrypted storage business context
ontology.owner_ref: CyberAlchemy v2 Knowledge Exchange Protocol product owner

nodes.label: Persist And Verify Encrypted Knowledge Material
nodes.meaning: The adopted reusable outcome for policy-bound immutable storage and verified retrieval of encrypted KEP material.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Consumer Owner
nodes.meaning: The owner of a consuming Product Capability that supplies semantic instantiation values without choosing runtime machinery.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Realization Owner
nodes.meaning: The later owner of provider, adapter, environment, configuration, and credential references.

nodes.label: Durable Knowledge Material Object
nodes.meaning: Immutable encrypted artifact or recipient-envelope bytes identified independently of provider and locator.

nodes.label: Content-Addressed Byte Identity
nodes.meaning: The domain- and algorithm-qualified identity of one exact stored byte sequence.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Binding
nodes.meaning: The versioned association between namespace, exact policy, and identified storage realization.

nodes.label: Storage Locator
nodes.meaning: A provider- or scheme-specific retrieval hint that never substitutes for byte identity.

nodes.label: Stored Recipient Envelope
nodes.meaning: Recipient-bound envelope bytes stored as an immutable durable object under exact identity and context.

nodes.label: Storage Write Receipt
nodes.meaning: A bounded observation that one realization accepted exact bytes; not proof of later retrieval or retention.

nodes.label: Verified Retrieval
nodes.meaning: A bounded retrieval whose returned bytes and required context match the requested object.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Policy
nodes.meaning: Immutable required behavior for retention, availability observation, redundancy, migration, deletion, and evidence.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Failure
nodes.meaning: A typed fail-closed result when an exact storage postcondition cannot be established.

nodes.label: Reissue-Safe Envelope Replacement
nodes.meaning: Write and verify a replacement envelope before changing the active commitment and retiring prior bytes.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Realization Identity
nodes.meaning: The exact evidence-bound identity of adapter, provider kind, environment, configuration schema, namespace, and build without credentials.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Evidence
nodes.meaning: An environment- and interval-bounded bundle of inputs, writes, retrievals, failures, migrations, state observations, and costs.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Infrastructure Cost
nodes.meaning: Storage expense that remains separate from knowledge price, seller payment, royalty, license, or owner compensation.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Confidentiality Boundary
nodes.meaning: Only encrypted bytes, public commitments, and necessary metadata may enter storage; plaintext, keys, and credentials remain outside.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Capability Instantiation
nodes.meaning: The consumer-owned semantic binding that reuses or specializes definitions and supplies every required policy value.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Input Contract
nodes.meaning: Requires exact object kind, bytes, qualified identity, namespace, policy, operation identity, and consumer instantiation.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Evidence Contract
nodes.meaning: Requires exact realization, binding, policy, operation inputs, write receipt, verified retrieval or typed failure, time interval, and cost observations.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Instantiation Context Policy
nodes.meaning: A consumer must bind all semantic storage slots before dependent use; provider realization remains separate.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Obligations
nodes.meaning: The closed rule and proof-requirement set for the reusable provider-neutral capability.

nodes.label: Durable Object Verified Retrievable
nodes.meaning: The exact encrypted object was accepted, retrieved, byte-verified, and context-verified under the named binding and policy.

nodes.label: Durable Storage Failure Bounded
nodes.meaning: A failed storage postcondition yields one typed failure and no dependent success claim.

nodes.label: Durable Envelope Reissue Safe
nodes.meaning: A replacement envelope is stored and verified before active commitment change while prior recoverability is preserved until commit.

ontology_type_selection.reason: This stage models the adopted Product Capability meaning; provider and runtime structure remain excluded.

proof_requirements.statement: Show exact bytes written and retrieved under one binding yield the same qualified byte identity.
Show changed, truncated, substituted, or context-mismatched bytes yield typed failure and no success.
Show a write receipt alone cannot satisfy verified readiness.
Show plaintext, unwrapped keys, private keys, and credentials are rejected from writes and evidence.
Show replacement is written and verified before commitment and prior bytes remain recoverable until commitment succeeds.
Show evidence changes identity when adapter, build, provider kind, configuration schema, namespace, endpoint class, locality, binding, or environment changes.
Show one observation cannot establish availability outside its named environment and interval.
Show storage costs remain separate from knowledge consideration in records and outcomes.
Show every consumer semantic slot is exact before a consumer DomainSpec or implementation binding can evaluate.

relations.meaning: The capability outcome is bounded to an exact verified retrieval.
The consumer owner supplies semantic bindings and policy values.
A separate owner binds provider and runtime realization identity.
Exact bytes determine object identity independently of location.
A locator helps resolution but never determines trusted identity.
Every operation resolves one exact policy version.
Evidence identifies the exact realization used by the binding.
A stored recipient envelope is one constrained durable object kind.
A write receipt observes acceptance of exact bytes without proving later availability.
Verified retrieval recomputes identity and checks required context.
Failure produces one typed bounded outcome rather than success.
Reissue replaces only the affected recipient envelope through the governed sequence.
The workflow outcome preserves recoverability until commitment succeeds.
Storage evidence preserves the exact write observation.
Storage evidence preserves byte- and context-verification results.
Negative cases remain first-class evidence.
Infrastructure cost remains visible and separate from knowledge consideration.
Stored objects contain encrypted material and allowed metadata only.
The consumer supplies every required semantic policy value.
The consumer declares the exact object kinds it uses.
No consumer operation proceeds with implicit semantic slots.
The output contract requires bounded evidence, not an unqualified success flag.
The context policy enforces semantic completeness before dependent use.

residue.description: DomainSpec v2 source requires exact admission of this business ontology.
residue.next_owner: Knowledge Exchange Protocol durable-storage Project owner

residue.description: No provider, adapter, endpoint, environment, region, or credential boundary is selected by this ontology.
Retention, availability observation, redundancy, migration, deletion, and recovery targets remain consumer-owned values.
Production cryptography, metadata privacy, traffic confidentiality, credential custody, and threat model need independent review.
The accepted Solana predecessor does not yet instantiate this capability; it requires a successor after generic construction is admitted.
residue.next_owner: Knowledge Exchange Protocol Solana capability owner

residue.description: No implementation binding or conformance evidence exists at the business-ontology stage.
residue.next_owner: Future durable-storage runtime and conformance owners

rules.failure_behavior: Reject mutation under the prior identity and require a successor object.
rules.statement: Any byte change creates a new Durable Knowledge Material Object identity.

rules.failure_behavior: Treat an unqualified or mismatched digest as ambiguous and fail closed.
rules.statement: Object identity includes domain, algorithm version, and digest of exact bytes.

rules.failure_behavior: Reject missing, stale, ambiguous, or policy-mismatched bindings.
rules.statement: Every operation binds one current namespace, policy version, and storage realization.

rules.failure_behavior: Reject locator-only trust and any digest mismatch.
rules.statement: A locator may change and may return candidate bytes; only qualified byte verification establishes object identity.

rules.failure_behavior: Keep readiness not_evaluable until a Verified Retrieval exists.
rules.statement: A successful write receipt is not proof of later retrieval, retention, or availability.

rules.failure_behavior: Emit typed storage failure and do not perform the dependent effect.
rules.statement: A consumer may perform its declared dependent effect only after exact byte and context verification under the current binding.

rules.failure_behavior: Return one closed failure code with bounded evidence.
rules.statement: Absent, unavailable, unauthorized, expired, mismatched, policy-mismatched, or ambiguous results never emit storage success.

rules.failure_behavior: Before commitment, preserve the prior envelope as active and recoverable.
rules.statement: Envelope reissue follows write replacement, verify replacement, commit active replacement, then policy-governed retirement of prior bytes.

rules.failure_behavior: Reject realization-collapsed object identifiers and migration claims.
rules.statement: Provider, adapter, namespace, endpoint, and locator are realization or binding facts, never immutable object identity.

rules.failure_behavior: Reduce the claim to observed facts and keep broader durability not_evaluable.
rules.statement: Every storage claim is bounded to the exact realization, binding, policy, environment, and observation interval.

rules.failure_behavior: Reject an economic record that collapses infrastructure cost into knowledge consideration.
rules.statement: Storage infrastructure cost remains distinct from knowledge price, seller payment, royalty, license consideration, and owner compensation.

rules.failure_behavior: Reject the write or evidence bundle and require security review.
rules.statement: Stored or evidenced material may contain encrypted bytes and allowed metadata but never plaintext, unwrapped content keys, private keys, or credentials.

rules.failure_behavior: Keep successor construction not_evaluable; never infer defaults or provider realization.
rules.statement: A consumer instantiation names every reuse or specialization and fills every required semantic slot before DomainSpec or implementation binding.
